changes.now: Frank fakes his death and tries to disappear into construction work. A hacker named Micro shows him the truth: his family died because of a CIA operation he served in, run by agent William Rawlins, and Frank's best friend, Billy Russo, was in on it. Frank kills Rawlins and leaves Russo's face scarred. The government clears him, and he walks free.
changes.proposed: Presumed dead, Frank tries to disappear into construction work. A hacker named Micro shows him the truth: his family died because of a CIA operation he served in, run by agent William Rawlins, and Frank's best friend, Billy Russo, was in on it. Frank kills Rawlins and leaves Russo's face scarred. The government clears him, and he walks free.
changes.evidence: Frank does not fake his death in The Punisher S1. He was reported dead after the Blacksmith's ship was destroyed in Daredevil S2; in S1 he is living as Pete Castiglione, and Micro (who is the one hiding behind a faked death) calls him 'Frank Castle, the dead man' after his 'reported demise' (S1E2 'Two Dead Men').

owner_calls.question: Miles's home universe is written as Earth-1610B (subjects stage 2, and status stage 4 'Miles: Spider-Man of Earth-1610B'). The films label it Earth-1610. Keep 1610B or use the on-screen Earth-1610?
options: Keep Earth-1610B (reference designation that tells it apart from the comics' Ultimate universe)
Change to Earth-1610, as labeled in Across the Spider-Verse (subjects stage 2 and status stage 4)
owner_calls.evidence: Wikipedia's Across the Spider-Verse plot: 'On Earth-1610, 16 months after the destruction of the Alchemax collider, Miles Morales...'. The '1610B' form does not appear on screen.
